text: Lin28a/b are RNA-binding proteins governing stem cell maintenance, metabolism, and oncogenesis, often overexpressed in poorly differentiated, aggressive cancers; their role in tumor initiation versus maintenance was unresolved. In murine models, LIN28B overexpression alone sufficed to initiate hepatoblastoma and hepatocellular carcinoma. Lin28b was also overexpressed in MYC-driven hepatoblastomas, and liver-specific Lin28a/b deletion reduced tumor burden, extended latency, and prolonged survival. Both intravenous Lin28b-targeting siRNA and conditional Lin28b deletion reduced tumor burden and prolonged survival, establishing a maintenance requirement. Mechanistically, Igf2bp proteins are upregulated, and Igf2bp3 is required for growth in the LIN28B-overexpression context. Across multiple murine models, Lin28b is sufficient to initiate liver cancer and necessary for its maintenance.
